title: The Big Sibling of AU Mic: A Cold Dust-rich Debris Disk around CP-72 2713 in the β Pic Moving Group
question: Characterize the newly identified cold debris disk around CP-72 2713 (size, dust and gas content, nature, stirring) using Spitzer, Herschel and ALMA 7-m data

evidence.quote: 8820 0.096±0.023 ATCA 10.6×10 [−][5] Norfolk et al. in prep.

what.value: Optical photometry from ASAS used for stellar SED

evidence.quote: we limited our analysis to data that are based on longer term monitoring observations taken from Kiraga (2012)
By adopting κ ν =2.3 cm [2] g [−][1] for the dust opacity (Andrews et al. 2013)

recipe.goal: Image ALMA continuum and fit ring model in uv plane
recipe.method: tclean continuum image; Gaussian ring (FWHM 0.2R) fitted to visibilities with uvmultifit after statwt
Grid of ring models convolved with alpha Boo PSF, Bayesian fit for R, PA, i
Spectrum extracted in disk mask (continuum SNR>2), rms scaled by √2.667, 3σ with linewidth 5 km/s
assumptions: CO co-located with dust; stellar mass 0.71 Msun

recipe.goal: SED fit for dust temperature and fractional luminosity
recipe.method: Single-temperature modified blackbody with λ0 fixed at 100 µm, iterative color corrections
assumptions: ATLAS9 photosphere, E(B-V)=0, solar metallicity, log g 4.5

recipe.goal: Derive dust and CO gas masses
recipe.method: Optically thin single-temperature dust mass; LTE optically thin CO mass upper limit for 10–45 K
assumptions: κν=2.3 cm2/g, grain temperature ~15 K at 140 au

recipe.goal: Collisional evolution modelling and stirring feasibility
recipe.method: ACE simulations of a 126–154 au belt with different wind rates; analytic stirring-onset models
assumptions: size distribution index -1.88, max 1e21 g, e=0.03, wind velocity 400 km/s
